title: Local Jacobian charts of a regular affinoid over a perfect field

proof.text: If $B=0$ the assertion is vacuous. Otherwise fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset B$, put $\mathfrak n\subset T$ to be its inverse image under $T\to B$, and identify $\kappa=T/\mathfrak n=B/\mathfrak m$. Put $P=F[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ and $\mathfrak p=P\cap\mathfrak n$. Apply [lem-trf-affinoid-polynomial-closed-point-comparison] with its polynomial ideal $J=0$. It says that $T$ is Noetherian, $\mathfrak p$ is maximal, and the induced map of completions $\widehat{P_{\mathfrak p}}\to\widehat{T_{\mathfrak n}}$ is an isomorphism. The field $F$ is Noetherian since each of its ideals is $0$ or $F$. Hence $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and both localizations are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], completing either local ring preserves its residue field. The completion isomorphism, being induced by $P_{\mathfrak p}\to T_{\mathfrak n}$, therefore identifies $P/\mathfrak p$ with $T/\mathfrak n=\kappa$ as $F$-algebras. For these maximal ideals, identifying the residue field of the localization with the quotient sends $g/u$ to $(u\bmod\mathfrak p)^{-1}(g\bmod\mathfrak p)$, and likewise for $T$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] makes $P/\mathfrak p$ finite-dimensional over $F$, since it is a field quotient of a polynomial algebra. Thus $\kappa/F$ is finite.

proof.text: The finite extension $\kappa/F$ of Step 1 is separable by the stated perfectness hypothesis. The definition [def-weil-regular-scheme] makes $B_{\mathfrak m}$ regular local. Therefore [lem-per-separable-regular-affinoid-residual-conormal] applies and gives injectivity of $d_{\mathfrak n}:I/\mathfrak n I\to\kappa^r$. This uses neither a discrete value group nor regularity after scalar extension.

proof.text: The classes $[f_j]$ span $I/\mathfrak n I$: reduce the coefficients in any expression $g=\sum_jb_jf_j$ modulo $\mathfrak n$. By [lem-weil-span-independent-subfamily], choose $E\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}$ whose classes are a basis. Injectivity in Step 2 shows that the matrix with columns $d_{\mathfrak n}([f_j])$, $j\in E$ in increasing order, defines an injective map $\kappa^E\to\kappa^r$: a vector in its kernel gives a zero basis combination in $I/\mathfrak n I$, so all its coordinates vanish.

proof.text: Put $S=T\setminus\mathfrak n$, $R=T_{\mathfrak n}$, and $M=S^{-1}I$, using [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The maximal ideal of $R$ is $\mathfrak nR$, and $M$ is finitely generated by the $f_j/1$. The formula $g/u\mapsto(u\bmod\mathfrak n)^{-1}[g]$ induces an isomorphism $M/\mathfrak nRM\simeq I/\mathfrak n I$. Indeed, a fraction equality becomes the same equality after reducing modulo $\mathfrak n$, since its witnessing multiplier is outside $\mathfrak n$; the formula kills $\mathfrak nRM$. Its inverse is $[g]\mapsto[g/1]$: if $v\in T$ lifts $(u\bmod\mathfrak n)^{-1}$, then $1-vu\in\mathfrak n$ and $g/u-vg/1=(1-vu)g/u$ vanishes modulo $\mathfrak nRM$. The two composites are consequently identities. The basis in Step 3 spans this quotient. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], $f_j/1$, $j\in E$, generate $M$.

proof.text:
For each $l\in\{1,\ldots,s\}$ express $f_l/1=\sum_{j\in E}(b_{lj}/u_{lj})(f_j/1)$ in $M$, with $u_{lj}
otin\mathfrak n$. Set $v_l=\prod_{j\in E}u_{lj}$. Multiplying gives an element $g_l=v_lf_l-\sum_{j\in E}c_{lj}f_j\in I$ whose localization is zero, with $c_{lj}\in T$. The zero criterion in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] supplies $w_l
otin\mathfrak n$ with $w_lg_l=0$. Thus $h_l=w_lv_l
otin\mathfrak n$ and $h_lf_l\in I_E$. The finite product $a=\prod_{l=1}^s h_l$ lies outside $\mathfrak n$, since $T/\mathfrak n$ is a field, and satisfies $af_l\in I_E$ for every $l$. By the definition of $I$ this gives $aI\subseteq I_E$, hence $a\in(I_E:I)$. All products over empty sets mean $1$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-injective-matrix-nonzero-maximal-minor] to the injective $r\times|E|$ matrix of Step 3. It supplies a subset $U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ of size $|E|$ with nonzero determinant in $\kappa$. The Leibniz formula in [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] commutes with reduction modulo $\mathfrak n$, term by term in its finite sum. The determinant in question is therefore $D_{E,U}\bmod\mathfrak n$, so $D_{E,U}\notin\mathfrak n$. This also covers $E=U=\varnothing$, whose determinant is $1$.

proof.text: In the field $\kappa=T/\mathfrak n=B/\mathfrak m$, both the image of $a$ from Step 5 and that of $D_{E,U}$ from Step 6 are nonzero. Their product is nonzero, giving $\bar a\,\bar D_{E,U}\notin\mathfrak m$. The choices are made separately at each maximal ideal, so $|E|$ may vary from point to point and no equidimensionality is used. If $I=0$, the basis may be empty, the colon element is $1$, and the argument gives the empty determinant. If $r=0$, the injection into $\kappa^0$ forces that same empty-basis case.
